body:
Clear colors on Linux X11 + NVIDIA as of 4.5.beta 2d113cc22 (reported by KColorChooser):

- Forward+, no HDR 2D: `#4c4c4c`
- Forward+, **HDR 2D**: `#4c4c4c` (same after a restart)
- Mobile, no HDR 2D: `#4c4c4c`
- Mobile, **HDR 2D**: `#4d4d4d` (same after a restart)
- Compatibility, no HDR 2D: `#4d4d4d`
- Compatibility, **HDR 2D**: `#4c4c4c` (same after a restart)


> Would it be catastrophic to change the default `default_clear_color` from 0.3 grey to 0.302 (0.30196079611778) so that the color will remain the same?

I would consider this acceptable personally, but maybe we can change the clear color setting rounding so be identical without changing the default.

cc @allenwp

> but maybe we can change the clear color setting rounding so be identical without changing the default. This might bite us in the arse if we ever support hdr output. I'd prefer changing the default color to exact srgb8 value more because it also gets rid of reset icon when you pick the "same" color. Current master:

The colour picker reports the default colour as `#4d4d4d`, which makes sense given 76.5 would normally be rounded up. `0.302` is a much nicer default, as this is a value that is close to one that you might actually choose from the colour picker.

Unfortunately, defaults are Godot's Achilles' heel for developing and improving the engine.

> maybe we can change the clear color setting rounding so be identical without changing the default.

This sounds even worse and hacky than changing the default to me.

I think the correct fix to an obviously unintentional inconsistency is the proposed one: changing the default to `0.302`. And I think the question in this issue is the right question to ask: would it be catastrophic?

...Put more accurately is: are there downsides that outweigh the benefits of changing the default in this case? To be thorough about it, we should consider the use cases:

- User looks at the default clear colour and notes that it is `#4d4d4d`
- Takes a screenshot
- Selects all of `#4d4d4d` in an art tool
- Confused that no pixels are selected

Another use case:

- User has some sort of post-processing that takes the 8-bit image and does something with the clear colour
- They can't find the clear color shown in the project settings because it's the default

These seem like reasonable use cases, though most of the time the user would actually change the clear colour to something that wouldn't be in their scene before doing this, so the default colour would not cause issue.

So it's a minor issue, but it is a bug for sure.

As for downsides? A user might already be doing something like that, but they have their code/process set to match the actual rendered colour of `#4c4c4c`. This change of default would break that behaviour.

I feel like I've already spent too much time trying to think through this extremely minor issue that is probably rare to cause problems in practice and I'd say that I lean a little more towards "This is a bug and the proposed fix is the correct fix, so let's just change the default to what it was intended to be in the first place. Probably nobody will notice or care."

> This might bite us in the arse if we ever support hdr output.

I don't see how this will be the case. I haven't done the math but I suspect it's just as likely that `0.3` sRGB will result in an awkward number for HDR colour spaces as `0.302` sRGB will. And selecting colours in HDR space is much less of a thing than in SDR sRGB (colours are typically handled as 16+ bit floating point, even in screenshots.)

Just took a brief look at the codebase and there are rather many places where the UI defaults are defined using simple floats. So, if there ever presents a time, like Godot 5 or other time UI can safely be overhauled, and someone has too much time in their hands, the default colors could all be converted to closest srgb8 derived value.

Could also be useful to have the documentation reflect that "this color is derived from srgb". Would be useful for web/constant colors and for the default `default_clear_color` - if we agree to change it now.

e.g.:
```html
<constant name="AQUAMARINE" value="Color(0.49803922, 1, 0.83137256, 1)">
to something like this:
<constant name="AQUAMARINE" value="Color8(127, 255, 212, 255)">
or this:
<constant name="AQUAMARINE" value="Color.hex(0x7FFFD4FF)">
```
